tasks.task: Find the course on Coursera named 'Essentials of Global Health'. Determine the instructor of this course and summarize his bio, note if there are any additional courses he offers on Coursera.
tasks.answer: The instructor of 'Essentials of Global Health' (Yale University) on Coursera is Richard Skolnik. Bio summary: Richard Skolnik has 40+ years of experience in international development and global health and authored the textbook 'Global Health 101'. He spent 25 years at the World Bank, retiring as Director for Health and Education for the South Asia Region, worked on health and education programs across Africa, the Middle East/North Africa, Latin America/Caribbean, and South Asia, served as VP for International Programs at PRB, Director of the Center for Global Health at The George Washington University, and Executive Director of the Harvard PEPFAR program for AIDS treatment in Botswana, Nigeria, and Tanzania. He served on the Global Fund's Technical Review Panel and WHO advisory groups, helped establish STOP TB, and was a Lecturer at the Yale School of Public Health and Yale School of Management. He holds a BA from Yale University and an MPA from Princeton's Woodrow Wilson School. Additional courses: Richard Skolnik offers NO additional courses on Coursera; his instructor profile 'Courses' section lists only 'Essentials of Global Health' (his course page also shows '1 Course').

tasks.task: Find a Coursera course on Sustainable Agriculture practices, and detail the course's objectives and the background of the lead instructor.
tasks.answer:
Course: Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (University of Florida) on Coursera (https://www.coursera.org/learn/sustainable-agriculture).

COURSE OBJECTIVES: The course covers agricultural and urban water quality issues in Florida, their bases, land and nutrient management strategies, and the science and policy behind best management practices (BMPs). Students will learn to evaluate BMP research and analyze its role in determining practices and policies that protect water quality. Skills gained include Environmental Issues, Water Resource Management, Water Resources, Environmental Regulations, Water Quality, and Land Management.

LEAD INSTRUCTOR BACKGROUND: George J. Hochmuth, Ph.D. - Professor at the University of Florida. He leads the Research Program in Urban and Agricultural Fertilization and Nutrient Management Practices. His research addresses environmental science questions about water quality and nutrient (especially nitrogen and phosphorus) and water management in urban and agricultural settings, including nutrient budgets in groundwater/surface water, alternative water sources for irrigation, efficient irrigation technologies, and improved water management practices to protect Florida's water quality.
